title: At least 930 people have died in Congo's Ebola outbreak - NPR
snippet: **At least 930 people have died in Congo's Ebola outbreak** **Congo's health ministry said the deaths were recorded out of the 2,344 cases confirmed as of Saturday. Thirty-seven new deaths were recorded in the previous 24 hours in one of the highest totals.**. # At least 930 people have died in Congo's Ebola outbreak. BUNIA, Congo — At least 930 people have died in Congo's Ebola outbreak, the country's Ministry of Health said Monday, with 37 new deaths recorded in a 24-hour span Friday into Saturday, one of the highest totals. The deaths were recorded out of the 2,344 cases confirmed as of Saturday, the health ministry said. The Bundibugyo virus responsible for the outbreak is less common than others that cause Ebola disease, and there is no approved vaccine or treatment. Congo's Health Ministry said in its latest update that 724 patients are currently in isolation and in hospitals, and that it is intensifying response efforts in affected health zones.

title: More health workers strike as Ebola cases in Congo exceed 2,000, including 754 deaths - Los Angeles Times
snippet: # More health workers strike as Ebola cases in Congo exceed 2,000, including 754 deaths. * Ebola cases in eastern Congo have surged past 2,000, with at least 754 deaths, in what authorities call the country’s fastest-growing outbreak fueled by the rare Bundibugyo strain. * Health workers at Bunia’s main hospital and other Ebola treatment centers have gone on strike over unpaid wages, even as more than 100 caregivers have been infected on the front lines. BUNIA, Congo — The number of confirmed cases of Ebola in Congo has reached 2,011, including 754 deaths, according to government data released overnight in what authorities say is the fastest-growing outbreak on record. Health workers at Bunia General Hospital, the region’s largest medical center, went on strike on Wednesday and are the latest group to have walked off their job at the epicenter over payment issues. The World Health Organization says more than 100 healthcare workers have been infected since the beginning of the outbreak.

title: Ebola outbreak: Uganda starts 42-day countdown to being declared free of the virus - BBC
snippet: # 'Moment of joy' as Uganda discharges last Ebola patient. The last patient being treated for Ebola in Uganda has been discharged from hospital, leaving the country with no active confirmed cases of the deadly disease. A 42-day countdown now begins before Uganda can officially be declared Ebola-free, as long as no new infections emerge. The first case in this outbreak of the Bundibugyo species of the virus in Uganda was confirmed in May. The patient was a man who had travelled from neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo, the outbreak's epicentre, for medical treatment. Speaking after Uganda's last Ebola patient left hospital, Health Minister Dr Chris Baryomunsi described it as "a moment of joy". Uganda has experienced several Ebola outbreaks over the last two decades and now has well established protocols to deal with the virus. It is thought that it could have been in the community undetected for months before the outbreak was officially declared two months ago.

title: Safety fears limit Ebola response in Congo, with at least 12 attacks recorded - Los Angeles Times
snippet: * At least a dozen attacks on Ebola treatment centers and health workers in Congo’s Ituri province are undermining containment efforts, raising fresh alarm over safety at the outbreak’s epicenter. * Unpaid local health staff members and other front-line workers have gone on strike, further slowing the response to the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record, with 2,181 cases and 864 deaths. BUNIA, Congo — At least a dozen attacks on health facilities and workers have been recorded during Congo’s Ebola outbreak, as safety fears restrict the response at the epicenter in Ituri province, authorities said Saturday. Many unpaid health workers and other front-line workers have gone on strike, further complicating response efforts in what’s been declared the fastest growing Ebola outbreak on record with 2,181 cases, including 864 deaths, so far recorded. Many of the attacks have been carried out by angry mobs who have stormed treatment centers or targeted response teams in the field, said Pierre Akilimali, incident manager for the Ebola response, at a news briefing in Bunia, the capital of Ituri.

title: DR Congo neighbors boost preparedness as Ebola cases surge - dw.com
snippet: The growing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is raising fears of regional spread, with Uganda, Rwanda and Zambia stepping up border screening, surveillance and emergency response measures. https://p.dw.com/p/5HQAy. Countries bordering the Democratic Republic of Congo have stepped up screening at border crossings, trained front-line health workers and activated emergency plans to reduce the risk of imported cases as the DRC battles a growing Ebola outbreak. The DRC has recorded 2,344 cases of Bundibugyo, the virus behind the current outbreak, which the government declared on May 15. Dr. Naeem Dalal, assistant director for preparedness and response at the Zambia National Public Health Institute (ZNPHI), told DW that prevention measures had been reinforced nationwide. The East African Community (EAC) has agreed on a coordinated response to improve preparedness and reduce the risk of cross-border transmission. EAC Secretary General Stephen Mbundi said partner states were working with the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC), the WHO and other partners to expand surveillance, laboratory testing and emergency response capacity.
